title: Human-in-the-Loop Review and Match Adjudication
objective: Give a human reviewer an efficient, well-instrumented way to adjudicate every match the system was not confident enough to auto-accept, and feed those decisions back into the system as reference data and quality measurement.
context_for_agent: The thresholds in stages 6 and 7 deliberately route the uncertain middle to human review rather than guessing. That design only works if reviewing is fast and well-supported — a review queue that is tedious to work will be rubber-stamped, which is worse than no review at all because it launders a low-confidence guess into a confirmed fact. Optimize for the reviewer making a correct decision quickly, and instrument the queue so rubber-stamping is detectable.

tasks.name: Review queue model
tasks.detail: Implement a queue over match candidates with review_status 'pending_review', ordered by a configurable priority: target urgency, match confidence (recommend reviewing the most ambiguous first, since those carry the most information), recency, and trajectory impact (a match that would connect two otherwise disjoint trajectory fragments matters more than a redundant one). Support claiming an item so two reviewers do not duplicate work, with claim expiry so abandoned claims return to the queue.

tasks.name: Review context assembly
tasks.detail: For each queued item, assemble everything the reviewer needs in one view: the candidate sighting's thumbnail at full available resolution, the target's reference images, the plate read with per-character confidence, the embedding similarity, the temporal and spatial context (what the trajectory looks like with and without this match), and the specific reason it fell into review. The comparison the reviewer must make is visual — make the two images directly comparable side by side at adequate size.

tasks.name: Adjudication actions
tasks.detail: Support: confirm (accept the match), reject (this is not the target), uncertain (defer with a note — never force a binary decision when the evidence genuinely does not support one), and flag-quality (the underlying image or read is unusable, which is distinct from the match being wrong and should feed a different metric). Every action records the actor, timestamp, decision, optional note, and time spent on the item.

tasks.name: Decision propagation
tasks.detail: On confirm: update match review_status, add the sighting as a reference embedding via stage 7's guarded path, and recompute the affected trajectory. On reject: exclude the sighting and recompute. Recomputation must be transactional and must record which trajectories changed as a result, so a decision's downstream consequences are visible rather than silent.

tasks.name: Bulk review
tasks.detail: Support reviewing several visually similar candidates together (e.g. successive frames of one track, or the same plate across nearby cameras) with a shared decision, since these are genuinely one judgment rather than many. Guard against over-broad bulk actions with a configurable maximum batch size and a required explicit confirmation showing every included item — bulk review is where rubber-stamping is most likely.

tasks.name: Reviewer agreement measurement
tasks.detail: Support optional double-review sampling: a configurable fraction of items is routed to two independent reviewers, and inter-reviewer agreement is measured (Cohen's kappa). Disagreements are surfaced for adjudication and are the most valuable signal available about where the system's thresholds sit relative to genuine human uncertainty.

tasks.name: Threshold feedback loop
tasks.detail: Aggregate review decisions into a labeled dataset and report: the confirm rate by confidence band (if items just below auto-accept are confirmed 99% of the time, the threshold is too conservative; if items just above are frequently wrong, it is too permissive), the reject rate by match method, and per-camera and per-condition quality issues. Provide scripts/analyze_review_decisions.py producing a recommended threshold adjustment with its supporting evidence. Recommend, do not auto-apply — a threshold change is a decision with consequences that deserves a human.

tasks.name: Rubber-stamp detection
tasks.detail: Instrument for the failure mode this stage exists to prevent: alert on implausibly short median review times, on confirm rates approaching 100% for a reviewer whose peers reject substantially more, and on bulk actions consistently at the maximum batch size. Surface these to administrators as a quality signal, not as an accusation.

tasks.name: Review UI
tasks.detail: Implement the reviewer interface following stage 17's design direction: side-by-side image comparison at maximum available resolution, keyboard shortcuts for every action (a reviewer working a queue should never need the mouse), the trajectory context rendered inline, and queue progress. Prefetch the next item so the interface never stalls between decisions.

tests_substage.description: Test both the mechanics and the safeguards. The safeguard tests matter most, because the mechanics failing is obvious while the safeguards failing is silent.

cases: items are ordered by the configured priority function
the most ambiguous items surface first under the recommended default ordering
a claimed item is not served to a second reviewer
an expired claim returns the item to the queue
claiming an already-claimed item fails cleanly with a clear message
releasing a claim returns the item immediately
an empty queue returns an empty state rather than raising
adjudicated items leave the queue
confirm sets review_status to confirmed and records the full decision record
reject sets review_status to rejected
uncertain leaves the item pending with the note attached and does not re-serve it immediately to the same reviewer
flag-quality records the distinct quality issue and is counted separately from a rejection
time-spent is recorded accurately using an injected clock
an action on an item claimed by another reviewer is refused
an action on an already-adjudicated item is refused
confirm adds the sighting as a reference embedding
confirm on a sighting with no embedding does not add a reference and does not raise
confirm triggers trajectory recomputation and the trajectory reflects the newly included sighting
reject triggers recomputation and the sighting is excluded
recomputation is transactional — a simulated failure mid-recompute leaves the prior trajectory intact
the set of changed trajectories is recorded and returned
confirming a match that changes nothing (already included) is a safe no-op
a bulk batch above the maximum size is rejected
bulk confirmation requires the explicit confirmation payload listing every item
a bulk action applies the decision to every included item
a bulk action failing partway is transactional — all or nothing
items in a bulk batch that were claimed by another reviewer are excluded and reported rather than silently included
the configured sampling fraction routes approximately that fraction to double review
two agreeing reviews produce agreement and no escalation
two disagreeing reviews are surfaced for adjudication
Cohen's kappa is computed correctly against hand-verified inputs including the perfect-agreement and chance-agreement edge cases
a reviewer never receives the same item twice in a double-review pair
an implausibly short median review time triggers the alert
a reviewer with a near-100% confirm rate against a peer baseline triggers the alert
consistent maximum-size bulk actions trigger the alert
a reviewer with normal patterns triggers no alert
each detection threshold is tested at its exact boundary
a search producing pending_review matches populates the queue
a reviewer claims, reviews, and confirms an item through the API, and the trajectory updates accordingly
the confirmed sighting becomes a reference embedding and improves subsequent matching for that target — asserted by measuring match results before and after
a rejected sighting is excluded from subsequent trajectories for that target
every review action appears in the stage 16 audit log with the correct actor
confirm rate by confidence band is computed correctly against a seeded decision set
a synthetic decision set where the threshold is clearly too conservative produces a recommendation to lower it, with supporting numbers
a synthetic set where it is too permissive produces the opposite recommendation
an ambiguous set produces no strong recommendation rather than a spurious one
recommendations are never auto-applied to configuration — explicitly asserted
the side-by-side comparison renders both images at full available resolution
every action is reachable by keyboard shortcut
the next item is prefetched and the interface does not stall between decisions
trajectory context renders inline with and without the candidate match
queue progress is accurate
two reviewers working the queue simultaneously never receive the same item
simultaneous adjudication attempts on one item resolve to exactly one winner
concurrent trajectory recomputation for the same target serializes correctly without corruption

exit_criteria: No item can be adjudicated by two reviewers simultaneously
Every decision propagates transactionally to trajectories and reference sets
Rubber-stamp detection triggers correctly on constructed patterns
Threshold recommendations are evidence-backed and never auto-applied
Every review action is audited with its actor
deliverables: docs/REVIEW.md documenting reviewer procedures and quality safeguards
